items.content_html:
The systemd v260 release has a new ModemManager integration for systemd-networkd. I've had a PR (#513521) merged for configuring the networkd side of things but found the following are needed in the nixos/modemmanager module:

  1. a new Polkit rule to allow systemd-networkd to communicate with ModemManager
  2. a way to start ModemManager.service automatically
    • (see also: #270809)

In testing this I've also found that the ModemManager.service does not stop cleanly and that changing the service KillMode=mixed fixes this (see man systemd.kill).

items.content_html:
This PR introduces a security.polkit.packages option. We have this types of option for dbus and systemd already, but for polkit you had to add the packages to environment.systemPackages with the side effect of cluttering up bin and other directories.

I have migrated some modules that contained a comment stating polkit was the only reason for including a package in systemPackages.

This is a breaking change that will affect some people, I have added a release note about this. A GitHub search shows about 50 cases, although some of those are likely manual forks and nixpkgs modules.

There isn't any test for polkit at the moment, but the rtkit test depends heavily on polkit, so I've used this to verify that the changes look okay.

items.content_html:
Generalises the existing --sudo handling into a small Elevator abstraction and adds a run0 backend, so activation commands on the local machine or a --target-host can be elevated via systemd's polkit-based run0 instead of sudo.
More backends could be added in the future without major rework.

--elevate {none,sudo,run0} selects the backend; --ask-elevate-password (-S) prompts locally and feeds the password to it. --sudo, --use-remote-sudo and --ask-sudo-password are kept as deprecated aliases.

For the local case, we run run0 -- <cmd> and the user's normal polkit agent (graphical or pkttyagent) handles any prompt.

For the remote case there is no controlling terminal over the SSH pipe, so the non-interactive systemd-run --uid=0 --pipe --wait ... form is used.
A transient unit does not inherit the SSH login environment, on NixOS its PATH is just the systemd store path, so the env-resolution shell wrapper runs in the login shell around systemd-run and forwards the resolved values into the unit via --setenv.
To express that, Elevator.wrap_remote() takes the env mapping and command and returns the full remote argv (sudo keeps the env wrapper inside itself, run0 puts it around).

Without --ask-elevate-password this relies on a polkit rule on the target granting the deploying user org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units (e.g. via security.polkit.extraConfig).

With --ask-elevate-password the remote command is wrapped in polkit-stdin-agent (new package), which registers a per-process polkit agent for the systemd-run child and answers the PAM conversation from stdin (there is no direct sudo --stdin equivalent for polkit).
On the target the agent is looked up as ${toplevel}/sw/bin/polkit-stdin-agent (falling back to the SSH login PATH), so it matches the target's architecture and nixpkgs revision rather than the deployer's.
The new system.tools.nixos-rebuild.enableRun0Elevation option puts it there via environment.systemPackages and enables polkit by default; since the toplevel is copied to the target before activation runs, this also works on the very first deploy.

I added a subtest to nixosTests.nixos-rebuild-target-host that tests the full --elevate=run0 --ask-elevate-password path end-to-end.

Supersedes #507054.
CC: @Jappie3
